title: VA Home Loan: Why the VA Home Loan Is Such a Valuable Benefit
summary:
VA is dedicated to empowering Veterans with access to one of the most important financial tools available today, the VA home loan benefit, which helps Veterans achieve homeownership with significant cost savings and long-term security.

Many Veterans may not realize they are eligible for one of the strongest homeownership benefits in the country. 
 
In part one of VA Home Loan series, Patrick Zondervan, Executive Director of Home Loan Guaranty, explains how the VA home loan works and why it is such an important benefit for Veterans and their families. 
 
The VA home loan program allows Veterans to purchase, retain, and adapt their homes with no down payment, no private mortgage insurance, and lower interest rates. 
 
The benefit can be used throughout a Veteran’s lifetime, creating opportunities for financial stability and long-term wealth. 

For assistance with VA’s home loan benefit, Veterans can call 1 877 827 3702 or visit https://www.va.gov/housing-assistance/home-loans/.

title: Farewell to Sam Faddis — Patriot, Truth Teller, and Friend
summary:
Farewell to Sam Faddis — Patriot, Truth Teller, and Friend

America has lost a friend and a patriot, and so have I. Sam Faddis—retired CIA operations officer, frequent guest on this show, and a man who became my friend even though I never met him in person—passed away quietly at the University of Pennsylvania in Philadelphia on the evening of July 25, 2026 with his wife, four children, and family by his side. I read the statement from his family, who asked for privacy and thanked the doctors, medical staff, and all of you for your prayers and support. I first came across Sam through Hillsdale College’s free Imprimis, where he wrote about what had gone wrong at the CIA and how to fix it—brave, objective, and always productive. Sam told the truth about everything, including how to right this ship. We’ll miss him terribly.

title: NJ MVC Software Error Registered 6,600 Non-Citizens to Vote—Why No Prosecutions?
summary:
NJ MVC Software Error Registered 6,600 Noncitizens to Vote—Why No Prosecutions?

Mark Garrett of Your LEO Nation reacts to a New Jersey press conference with Lieutenant Governor Caldwell and MVC acting chair Rosalie Johnson, where the governor disclosed a serious MVC software error that allegedly improperly registered about 6,600 noncitizens to vote between June 2023 and June 2024, with an initial analysis indicating fewer than 400 of those individuals voted. Garrett says the governor is using “accountability” language while blaming predecessors and Donald Trump, but failed to include any prosecutors on stage and showed no intent to prosecute those who voted illegally—an indictable third-degree offense carrying 3–5 years and up to $15,000 in penalties.
